transcript.content: Hello, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… thanks for seeing me. I guess I’m here because things at work kind of got away from me. I’m an industrial production manager, and for a while I was taking on a lot—like launching plant redesign projects one after another, calling suppliers after hours, rewriting the shift plan myself… I thought I was just being productive, maybe a little too enthusiastic.

But then it sort of flipped, and I couldn’t keep up with all the plans I’d put in motion. It’s embarrassing to say, because I’m usually very organized, but I started feeling like I’d created more than I could manage. Does that make sense?
During that highly productive period, did you need much less sleep than usual and still feel rested?

Yeah… I mean, I probably would’ve said at the time that I was just “running efficiently,” but yes. I was only sleeping maybe two or three hours some nights and still going into the plant feeling really sharp and charged. Like sleep was optional, or kind of… inefficient. I know that probably sounds off.
During that time, did you feel unusually confident or powerful, like you could handle things other people couldn’t?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I wouldn’t have called it “powerful” at the time, exactly. More like I was just very sure I understood the plant better than anyone else.

But honestly… I did believe I could fix the entire production workflow faster than the consulting team we had, and I kind of brushed off people’s concerns because failure just didn’t seem like a real possibility to me. Saying it now, it sounds arrogant, doesn’t it? I didn’t mean it that way at the time.
During that energized period, were you hospitalized because of your behavior or mental state?

No… I wasn’t hospitalized. It didn’t get to that point, as far as I understand it. People were concerned, and work became… messy, but no one took me to a hospital or anything like that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During that energized period, did you have beliefs that other people said were unrealistic or not true?

I guess… yes, in a way. I don’t think I was believing something impossible, exactly, but people did tell me I was being unrealistic.

I honestly thought I could fix the whole production workflow faster than the consulting team, like I just saw it more clearly than everyone else. And when people raised concerns, I kind of dismissed them because… at the time, failure didn’t really feel like an option. Or even a real possibility.

I know that probably sounds bad. I’m not trying to make myself sound better than I was.
During that energized period, did you hear or see things that other people said were not there?

No… I don’t think so. Not like hearing voices or seeing things that weren’t there.

I was maybe overly focused and convinced about what I was doing, but I don’t remember anyone saying I was seeing or hearing things. That didn’t happen, as far as I know. Is that the distinction you’re asking about?
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day, or lost interest in most things you usually enjoy?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, but lately it’s been pretty constant.

I wake up in the temporary apartment with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day is already ruined before I even drive to the plant. Most days it’s there right away. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of “depressed most of the day” you mean, but… it feels like it probably is.
During that low period, did you lose interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean… I still did some things, so it wasn’t like I stopped functioning completely.

But if you mean actually enjoying them, or wanting to do them the way I normally would… I guess I haven’t really noticed much of that. It’s more like I go through the motions. I don’t know if that counts.
During that low period, did you have times when you felt worthless or excessively guilty?

I’m… not sure I’d put it as “worthless.” That sounds kind of strong.

I do get really down on myself, like I should be handling everything better or I’m letting people down somehow. But I don’t know if that’s excessive guilt, or just… normal guilt when you’re not doing your best. Does that count, or is that different from what you mean?
During that energized period, did your behavior cause serious problems at work or in your relationships?

I… I guess yes, though I hate saying it that way because I don’t want it to sound like I was causing chaos on purpose.

There was a shift-planning meeting where I just couldn’t keep up or make the calls I was supposed to make, and I had to ask to be pulled out of it. And then occupational health got involved because I wasn’t really able to carry out the basic production decisions my job depends on.

So… yes, I think it did cause serious problems at work. I’m sorry, is that the kind of thing you mean?
